title: Bisected simulated embryos regenerate the full target form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bisected simulated embryos regenerate the full target form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When the partially differentiated simulated embryo is cut in two and each half's cells are replicated, the cells undergo slight dedifferentiation and then each half regenerates the complete head–body–tail target morphology, illustrating pluripotency and recovery from drastic interventions in the active-inference model.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This example illustrates the pluripotential nature of the cells and the ability of self-assembly to recover from fairly drastic interventions.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis”. Scope: Active-inference morphogenesis simulation (analogous to planarian or regulative embryo bisection)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is restricted to a specified intervention in a small simulation and can be directly reproduced. Its biological analogy should not be conflated with the resolvable computational result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At simulation step eight, bisect the ensemble, duplicate cells in each half, and quantify dedifferentiation and final recovery of the complete target arrangement. Failure of either half to recover under the specified model refutes the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: The simulated replication operation is an abstraction of biological bisection.

operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data existence: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bisection, duplication, and re-integration are implemented in the same public file that the paper identifies as the reproduction route. Turning on the existing flag and scoring return to the target is a rerun. The flag's default and the updated target mask are the main limits on an exact figure match.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enable the script's half-split path, which copies the upper or lower half of a partially differentiated ensemble at time step 8 and continues integration. Recovery of the full target by both halves confirms the reported regeneration result; a half that stays truncated or fails to redifferentiate refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The default target is no longer the paper's head–body–tail embryo.

The split path is present but switched off in the current file, so the run needs that flag set.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.76
operationalizability: 0.88
data existence: 0.86
data adequacy: 0.74
analysis feasibility: 0.78

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, if morphogenesis is run for 8 steps, the embryo is cut into a head half and a tail half, each half's cells are replicated (keeping location and partial differentiation) and each half is integrated separately for 32 more steps, then both halves regenerate the full head-body-tail target, after a transient dedifferentiation.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, over 20 random seeds: after the split and 32 further steps, both halves meet the assembly criterion of levin-2015-place-01 (RMS position error under best one-to-one assignment < 0.5 x smallest target spacing, and >= 7/8 cells correctly typed) in at least 16 of 20 runs; and dedifferentiation is seen, i.e. in the majority of runs, for at least one half, mean max identity probability falls below its value at the split during the first 8 post-split steps.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: fewer than 10 of 20 runs have both halves meeting the assembly criterion. Between 10 and 15 is 'mixed'; full regeneration without any measured dedifferentiation dip is reported as supporting the regeneration part and not the dedifferentiation part ('mixed' if the dip criterion fails).
